analysis.title: National Vision Holdings (EYE): Takeaways from virtual group meeting with CEO and CFO
key_insights: GS hosted a virtual group meeting on Nov 17, 2026 with National Vision CEO Alex Wilkes, CFO Chris Laden and IR head Tamara Gonzalez. Topics were 3Q traffic and ticket drivers, the implied 4Q SSS deceleration, and profitability initiatives.

GS maintains Neutral on EYE. It is encouraged by management's revenue and profit initiatives but stays on the sidelines because of accelerating traffic declines and competitive concerns as EYE leans into higher-income, managed care customers.

3Q ticket growth was +8.9% while traffic fell 5.6%. Management calls the softness in lower-value transactions a deferral issue rather than a share loss. Repeat-customer purchase cycles lengthened by about 3 weeks in 3Q, versus about 2 weeks in 2Q.

The bottom 25% of transactions by ticket value are only high-single-digit % of total sales and a lower share of gross profit. Management expects lower-value transactions to become a tailwind once purchase cycles normalize.
Marketing is shifting to also reach higher-value consumers, while value offers such as the 2 for $95 bundle are still aimed at cash-pay customers.

3Q ticket growth was two-thirds mix and one-third price. Price came mostly from contact lenses, as manufacturer price increases flowed through. Frames and lenses saw both price and mix gains, from a more modern frame assortment and premium lens materials and add-ons.
Management said EYE improved in every product category that was underpenetrated last year, including transitions, premium materials and anti-reflective coatings.

FY26 guidance implies 4Q SSS decelerates on a 2-year stack. Management attributes this to a cautious volume outlook and to lapping pricing launched in 4Q25. FY26 ticket growth should be a balance of price and mix, versus price-heavy in 2025.

Management expects SSS to be largely ticket-driven for the next few years. It should become more balanced between traffic and mix over time as marketing broadens beyond entry-level cash-pay customers and store growth re-accelerates, with 50-55 openings expected in FY27.
Managed care is about 42% of revenue, up 1.5-2pp y/y. EYE uses everyday low pricing, versus peers' high-low model, and management sees a potential long-term managed care mix of 50%.

In 4Q, management expects ticket deceleration to come from lapping price increases, not lower attachment rates. Mix into premium frames and lens add-ons carries a lower gross margin rate, and 4Q will also lap a modest gross margin benefit from better managed care collection rates in 4Q25.

A new labor scheduling platform and an agile operating model were rolled out to about 150 lower-volume stores. Multi-skilled staff replace position-specific specialists so these stores run with fewer employees.

Management views the optometrist environment positively. Remote capabilities make EYE more attractive to graduating optometrists, and a shift to higher-value transactions should reduce pressure on doctors to raise patient visits.

YTD 2026 buybacks are $52mn versus $2.6mn a year earlier. A further $100mn repurchase authorization through Dec 2030 took effect Nov 9. Management will give more detail with 2027 guidance and plans balanced capital allocation.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $24 12-month target based on 8.0x/9.0x/10.0x downside/base/upside EV/EBITDA. It cites accelerating traffic declines and competition as EYE moves toward higher-income managed care customers.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported): ticket growth +8.9%, customer traffic -5.6%, SSS positive and ticket-led. Mix was two-thirds and price one-third of ticket growth.
FY26 company guidance implies a 4Q SSS deceleration on a 2-year stack. Management cites a cautious volume outlook and lapping 4Q25 pricing.

GS estimates (forecast): EPS $0.80 for 12/25, $1.01 for 12/26E, $1.17 for 12/27E and $1.37 for 12/28E. Revenue is $1,987.5mn for 12/25 and $2,028.2mn, $2,126.9mn and $2,297.6mn for 12/26E-12/28E. EBITDA is $192.9mn for 12/25 and $224.4mn, $253.2mn and $280.7mn for 12/26E-12/28E.
GS quarterly EPS estimates (forecast): $0.30 for 9/26, $(0.00) for 12/26E, $0.51 for 3/27E and $0.18 for 6/27E.
FY27 store openings are expected at 50-55. Management will give 2027 guidance at a later date.
risk_factors: Upside risks: better-than-expected eye care and eyeglasses demand, a meaningful acceleration in trade-down, faster margin recovery, and a multiple re-rating if sentiment improves on better top-line results and a clear path to margin recovery.

Downside risks: a slower top-line recovery as lower-income and uninsured customers defer demand or exit the market, less trade-down, continued exam capacity headwinds, margin pressure from higher wages, more competition, and persistently elevated costs.
Mix shift toward premium frames and lens add-ons carries lower gross margin rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Management sees weak lower-value transactions as a deferral issue, with repeat purchase cycles about 3 weeks longer, and expects a tailwind once cycles normalize. Ticket growth of +8.9% is led by mix, and managed care is gaining share toward a possible 50% mix.
tension_points.bear_case: GS cites accelerating traffic declines (-5.6% in 3Q) and competitive risk as EYE leans into higher-income managed care customers. FY26 guidance implies a 4Q SSS deceleration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slower top-line recovery as lower-income and uninsured customers defer demand or exit the market, as named in GS's downside risks.
